title: Minimum Recolors to Get K Consecutive Black Blocks
statement:
The string `blocks` describes a row of blocks: `blocks[i]` is `'W'` if block `i` is white and `'B'` if it is black. One operation paints a single white block black (black blocks cannot be changed).

Given an integer `k`, return the fewest operations needed so that the row contains `k` black blocks next to each other somewhere. If such a run already exists, the answer is `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

The `k` black blocks must sit in some window of `k` consecutive positions, and making a window all black costs exactly its number of white blocks. So the answer is the smallest white count over all windows of length `k`. Recounting each window costs O(nk); sliding the window one step only adds one block on the right and drops one on the left, so the count can be updated in O(1).

## Approach

1. Count the white blocks in the first window, positions `0` to `k - 1`, into `whites`; set `best = whites`.
2. Move the window right one step at a time: `right` is the block entering, `right - k` the block leaving.
3. Add 1 to `whites` if the entering block is white, subtract 1 if the leaving block is white.
4. Keep the smallest `whites` seen in `best` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`blocks = "WBBWWBBWBW"`, `k = 7`. The first window `"WBBWWBB"` has `whites = 3`, so `best = 3`.
- `right = 7` brings in `W` and drops the `W` at 0: `whites = 3`.
- `right = 8` brings in `B` and drops the `B` at 1: `whites = 3`.
- `right = 9` brings in `W` and drops the `B` at 2: `whites = 4`.

The smallest count is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each block enters and leaves the window once.
- Space: O(1): only counters.

## Pitfalls

- When `k` equals the length of `blocks` there is just one window; the sliding loop never runs and the first count is the answer.
- The leaving block is at `right - k`, not `right - k + 1`; an off-by-one makes the window the wrong size.
- Count whites, not blacks: the cost is the number of blocks that need painting.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `whites` | white blocks inside the current window of length `k` |
| `best` | smallest white count over the windows seen so far |
| `right` | index of the block entering the window |

narration.2: whites will hold the number of white blocks in the current window.
narration.3: Build the first window from positions 0 to k - 1.
narration.4: Every white block in it would need one repaint.
narration.6: The first window's cost is the best so far.
narration.7: Slide the window: block right enters on the right.
narration.8: A white block entering adds one repaint.
narration.9: The block at right - k leaves; if it was white, one repaint is no longer needed.
narration.12: The cheapest window is the fewest repaints needed.
